ownership_reason: Only the gold walks the chain of property accesses of an assignment target and decides on its root; hops 1-3 hold the function and its parent, hop 4 the target, and each gets back a name or null. The gold returns null for the whole of this.a and no sub-node of it has a qualified name (the property is a STRING node), so no hop can call the gold on another node or wrap its result to obtain this.a; restoring it outside the gold needs a second walk over the chain (or Node.getQualifiedName, which replaces the gold). The convention is pinned outside the gold: Node.getQualifiedName names THIS 'this', so this.a is 'this.a', and Node.isQualifiedName documents 'such as x or a.b.c or this.a' (NodeTest.testIsQualifiedName asserts this.foo); NodeUtil.getRootOfQualifiedName says the root must be either NAME or THIS; NodeUtil.getFunctionName, beside the facade and used by five production passes, names an assigned function by the target's Node.getQualifiedName; NodeNameExtractor.getName names THIS 'this' when naming anonymous functions (NameAnonymousFunctionsTest.testAssignmentToGetElem); SourceMapGeneratorV1Test.testFunctionNameOutput2 pins that a function assigned to a.b.c is named a.b.c. The gold's javadoc promises the qualified name of the expression, which this.a has.
